thread:
Maria L.: Pasted apples-to-apples run for a set of customer prompts + identical decoding params. Seeing a weird perf delta between model-A-quant and model-B-quant even though token counts match. Results attached inline. :thinking:

Maria L.: Summary: model-A-quant avg latency 42ms/token, model-B-quant 58ms/token (95th shows same gap). Cost roughly +35% for model-B. Throughput tests were done with replay harness (same inter-arrival distribution).

perf-bot: CI perf-check finished: 1769004330 - harness run id: rh-20260318-88 - status: complete - metrics: tokens=1.2M, tail=95th: 62ms, p50: 21ms

Aj T.: Did we confirm tokenizer alignment? small mismatches in tokenization will change kv-cache reuse and effective sequence lengths.

Maria L.: Good call. I re-ran with tokenizer-normalized inputs (lowercase + unicode normalize + HF tokenizer). Gap narrows but still ~20% delta. So tokenizer mismatch explains part, not all.

Simon K.: Could be kernel selection. Model-B is triggering generic attention kernel because sequence distribution trips the heuristic for fused attention. Do we have the kernel trace?

Maria L.: Attached trace snippet from runtime profiler:

```
[trace] kernel_candidates: [fused_attn_fp16, generic_attn_q8, block_sparse_attn]
[trace] selected: generic_attn_q8 (score: 0.31)
[trace] exec_time(ms): generic_attn_q8=0.42, fused_attn_fp16=0.28 (est)
[trace] kv_cache_hits: 0.72, avg_prefix_len: 12
```

Maria L.: Notice the estimator favored generic due to memory pressure estimate. But actual run shows fused would have been faster. Looks like estimator weights need tuning for q8 paths.

Kevin P.: Hmm. Could the batching heuristics be mis-predicting tail-latency tradeoffs? The replay harness batches by a 10ms window, but live traffic has spikes. If fused has worse memory but better compute, the estimator should prefer it for seq<32. What's the sequence distribution in this run?

Maria L.: Sequence histogram: 0-8: 28%, 9-32: 51%, 33-64: 15%, >64: 6%. So most are small.

Aj T.: If most are <=32, fused should almost always win. Might be an interaction with KV cache warming: model-B uses slightly different tokenization so fewer prefix hits early in stream -> lower effective reuse -> higher memory per request -> estimator picks generic. We should simulate cold-start vs warmed runs.

Olivia R.: Can we reproduce with a controlled replay: same prompts but forcing consistent tokenizer and toggling kv_cache enabled/disabled? Also seed sampling for randomness in batching.

Maria L.: I ran three quick variants: (1) tokenizer aligned + kv enabled (current) -> 58ms avg
(2) tokenizer aligned + kv disabled -> 63ms avg
(3) tokenizer aligned + kv enabled + prewarm replay (prefix warmup phase of 2000 tokens) -> 44ms avg

Maria L.: So prewarming KV cache collapses most of the gap. That suggests model-B is sensitive to cache warmup and the kernel heuristic overestimates memory cost during cold cache.

Simon K.: Action: update kernel selection scoring to include a dynamic kv_reuse factor coming from recent traffic samples (last N requests). If reuse > 0.6 prefer fused. I'll sketch a PR.

Kevin P.: Also propose an A/B in the replay harness: run an apples-to-apples where we inject warmup phase vs no-warmup to surface real-world difference. We'll use the same arrival pattern used in prod to be realistic.

Aj T.: Small note on apples-to-apples: ensure decoding params identical AND stop sequences enforced by same post-processing. In past we saw hidden whitespace differences cause different early termination rates which skews token counts.

Maria L.: Agreed. I included exact decoding JSON in the run header and postproc commit hash.

perf-bot: perf-alert: regression detected for model-B-quant vs baseline on branch main - delta p50 +18ms - investigate: https://perf.redwood/runs/rh-20260318-88

Olivia R.: Who will own the follow-ups? I can take reproducer harness (warmup vs cold) and provide a short writeup. Simon, can you do the kernel scoring tweak? Aj, can you add tokenizer-normalization step to the apples-to-apples pipeline?

Simon K.: Yep, I'll open a draft PR for scoring changes and add a flag to simulate kv_reuse in the estimator.

Aj T.: I'll add normalization and a test that fails if tokenization changes between models for the same input.

Maria L.: Thanks all. I'll update the perf run with new configs and loop back with fresh numbers. :thumbsup:

Kevin P.: Follow-up: after fixes let's run a 24h replay with production-shaped bursts to confirm no regression in tail latency when preferring fused kernels.

Maria L.: Noted. Will schedule.

perf-bot: scheduled run rh-20260319-01 queued by Maria L.

Maria L.: End of thread notes: root cause = kernel estimator + KV cache warmup interaction + tokenizer alignment caveats. Next steps assigned.
